title: Writing: A Persuasive Essay on an Environmental Issue

writingModel.placeholder: State the issue clearly and present your position — use an emphasis structure to signal importance
writingModel.hint: "It is X that represents the greatest challenge." / "What we face is…"

writingModel.placeholder: First argument with evidence — use a participle clause to connect cause and effect
writingModel.hint: e.g. "Powered by fossil fuels… / Having failed to act earlier…"

writingModel.placeholder: Second argument — acknowledge the counter-argument and refute it
writingModel.hint: Use contrast linkers: "Although some argue… / Despite concerns about cost…"

writingModel.placeholder: Third argument — use emphasis structures for impact
writingModel.hint: "What is needed is… / Never before has… / It is not X but Y that…"

writingModel.placeholder: Conclude with a call to action and forward-looking statement
writingModel.hint: "Only by acting now can we… / What the future requires is…"

writingTemplate.suffix: that represents the most urgent environmental challenge of our time.
writingTemplate.placeholder: the failure to price carbon emissions / the lack of political will on climate action
writingTemplate.hint: It-cleft to open — immediately signals what the argument will be about

writingTemplate.suffix: , industrialised nations bear a particular responsibility to lead.
writingTemplate.placeholder: produced the majority of historical emissions / benefited from fossil-fuel-powered growth
writingTemplate.hint: Perfect participle: prior action creates current responsibility

writingTemplate.placeholder: some argue the transition is too expensive / clean energy investment creates more jobs than it destroys

writingTemplate.prefix: What the data makes clear is
writingTemplate.placeholder: that the cost of inaction far exceeds the cost of action
writingTemplate.hint: Wh-cleft for emphasis on the key finding

writingTemplate.suffix: can we hope to limit warming to 1.5 degrees.
writingTemplate.placeholder: acting with the urgency the science demands / achieving net zero by 2050
writingTemplate.hint: "Only by… can we…" = inversion + strong call to action

items: It is not X but Y that we must address.
What the evidence clearly shows is…
Never before has the need for action been more urgent.
Only by [action] can we [outcome].
It is [this] that determines whether we succeed or fail.
Powered by fossil fuels for two centuries, the global economy now faces a critical transition.
Having failed to act earlier, we now face much steeper costs.
Designed to incentivise clean investment, carbon pricing shifts market behaviour.
Driven by consumer demand and government policy, the EV market is growing rapidly.
Threatened by rising seas, island nations have the strongest moral claim to climate finance.
Although some argue that the transition is too costly…
Despite concerns about economic disruption…
Critics point out that… However, the evidence suggests…
It is sometimes claimed that… Nevertheless, the data shows…
While it is true that… this does not negate the fact that…
What we owe future generations is not perfection but decisive action.
Only by treating this as the emergency it is can we prevent the worst.
It is not technology but political will that we lack.
Never in human history has a generation had both the knowledge and the means to prevent catastrophe — and faced the choice of whether to use them.
The question is not whether we can act, but whether we will.

questions.text: "___ governments ___ urgent action that will determine the future of the climate." (it-cleft)
questions.hint: "It is + X + that + verb…" = it-cleft emphasising governments

questions.text: "___ (benefit) from fossil fuels for decades, wealthy nations have an obligation to lead the transition."
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action creates current obligation

questions.text: "___ the cost of inaction is ___ the evidence consistently shows." (wh-cleft emphasising "the cost")
questions.hint: "What [the evidence shows] is [the cost of inaction]" = wh-cleft

questions.text: "___ by acting decisively now ___ we limit the damage to future generations." (inversion after "only")
"___ by rising seas, the Maldives has called on wealthy nations to honour their climate finance commitments."
"Never the planet has warmed so rapidly" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "Never before has the planet warmed…" — inversion: auxiliary before subject

questions.text: "It is not the lack of technology ___ limits progress, but the absence of political will."
questions.hint: "It is not X that… but Y" = negative it-cleft

questions.text: "___ investing in clean energy significantly outweigh the costs of inaction." (emphasis — the benefits)
opts: What is clear is that the benefits of
It is clear that benefits of
questions.correct: What is clear is that the benefits of
questions.hint: "What is clear is that…" = wh-cleft for emphasis
